MAINTENANCE · Mechanical

Vehicle Modifications in Riyadh

Considered, workshop-assessed vehicle modifications for premium cars in Riyadh — discussed case by case, with honesty about what suits the car and what is feasible.

  1. Home
  2. Maintenance
  3. Vehicle Modifications

Modification requests on premium vehicles deserve an engineering conversation, not a catalogue upsell. Some upgrades suit a platform well; others compromise reliability, safety systems, or regulatory compliance. QSC treats modifications as case-by-case projects: the workshop hears what you want to achieve, assesses the specific vehicle, and tells you plainly what it will and will not do — including when the honest answer is 'we advise against it'.

The best modification projects start with a use case, not a parts list: more comfort for a daily commute, retrofitting a factory feature the car shipped without, protecting a new vehicle's paint and interior, preparing a GT car for long highway trips. When the goal is clear, the engineering follows honestly — which options genuinely serve it, what each costs in money and in side effects, and where the factory solution beats the aftermarket one. QSC runs that conversation before quoting anything, because a modification that solves the wrong problem is just expensive clutter.

Factory-option retrofits deserve their own mention: many desirable features — cameras, parking aids, comfort and convenience functions — exist as unpopulated provisions in these vehicles, and installing genuine hardware with correct coding yields a result indistinguishable from factory build. It is the most reversible, value-neutral class of modification there is. Conversely, QSC is frank about modifications that hurt: anything compromising safety systems, emissions compliance or structural integrity gets a clear 'we advise against it', with the reasons.

FAQ

Frequently asked questions

Do you do performance tuning?

Performance-related requests are discussed individually — the answer depends on the platform, the specific change and its implications. QSC does not publish blanket promises about power figures.

Will modifications affect my warranty or insurance?

They can. Review your warranty and insurance terms before modifying; the workshop will tell you which changes are commonly sensitive, but the contractual judgement belongs to your providers.

Can you return a modified car to standard?

Usually yes, depending on what was changed and parts availability. Bring the car's modification history if you have it — the assessment is more accurate with it.

Can you install accessories I bought myself?

Usually yes, after checking two things: that the parts suit your exact vehicle, and that installation will not disturb systems the part touches. Bring the parts or send their details before the appointment — discovering incompatibility on the lift wastes your booking.
